maya: Heads-up — proposal to add a tiny provenance header on edge proxies so downstream ingest can do deterministic attribution even when sampling / batching happens at the edge. Sketch below, want quick sanity check before I open an RFC.

maya: Problem: we lose stable attribution for traces/metrics when edge sampling or batching drops or compacts attributes. That makes cost attribution fuzzy, and late-enrich lookups are expensive.

maya: Proposal (lightweight): add `x-rdwd-prov` header with a compact base64 payload: `v1:<cohort_id>:<partial-key-hash>` where cohort_id ~= 6 chars, partial-key-hash ~= 10 chars. Example: `v1:c3r7a:9f2bd4a1c2`

maya: nginx snippet we tested locally:```add_header X-Rdwd-Prov "$prov";``` where `$prov` is set by lua that picks/randomizes cohort and computes 40-bit siphash over billing key.```

jun: quick q: why embed hash vs just an opaque short id we resolve later?

maya: two tradeoffs: opaque id => must call back to a resolution service for every sampled event -> very high QPS. Hash provides local cheap join for most queries (probabilistic) and lets late-enrich service be best-effort for ambiguous hits.

ravi: concerns: header growth and mobile MTU. Are we sure ~30 bytes is safe on all carriers? Also encryption/sensitivity — could this leak tenant info?

maya: agreed. design constraints I had in mind: keep header <= 40 bytes, no raw tenant IDs, only salted hash+cohort. Salt rotates per region (config) and we sign with ephemeral key to avoid easy enumeration.

jun: operationally, how do we handle churn — cohort reassignment? We need deterministic cohort assignment so cached aggregated metrics don't flip.

maya: cohorts are stable per install for 30d by default; assignment is hash(billing_key||region||epoch) truncated to 24 bits then encoded base32. Epoch only increments on explicit migration windows.

taylor: rollout plan idea: start in EU edge fleet read-only (set header but no ingest-side indexing), measure cardinality and false positive rate by sampling full keys at low rate. If FP << 0.5% we can enable full joins.

ravi: how will this interact with prefix compression/kv caching in runtime? We may need to propagate prov header into prefix-cache keys or the cache will serve responses without attribution tags.

maya: good call — runtime should stash prov header in the request context and ensure responses include it for any caching telemetry emitted. We can add a small variant tag on cache keys: `cachekey|provcohort`. Overhead is tiny since cohorts are compact.

jun: metrics we should track during canary: cohort-cardinality, prov-header-presence-rate, late-enrich-lookup-qps, enrich-miss-rate, and attribution-precision (measured via full-key-sampled ground truth).

maya: exactly. Also SLA for the resolution service: 10ms P95 target, fallback to probabilistic attribution if resolution unavailable. We need graceful degradation.

taylor: who owns the resolution and cache? eng-platform or eng-runtime? I vote eng-platform runs the service, runtime integrates client for local cache + metrics tags.

ravi: runtime integration is small — we can add a local LRU for cohort -> billingkey mappings for short TTL (5m) to cut latency. But lifecycle + privacy checks should be in platform service.

maya: open questions I want calls on before RFC: 1) header format final (v1 vs hex vs base32) 2) cohort size & TTL 3) signed vs unsigned OK 4) how to surface this to customers (opt-in vs default)

jun: my 2c: base32 compact, signed, default-on for hosted but opt-in for private installs. Add a governance flag for regulated customers to disable.

ravi: agree with default-on hosted. For private we need a config toggle + doc that warns about privacy tradeoffs. Also add a migration tool for epoch bumps.

taylor: I'll draft a rollout runbook: canary -> staged fleet -> ingest-side indexing -> enable joins -> monitor for FP/regressions. Add an abort path to remove header from proxies quickly if we hit carrier issues.

ingest-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://go/redwood/infra/edges/prov-rollout-checklist (internal) :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks — I'll incorporate this feedback, add the runbook & metrics to the RFC, and solicit legal on privacy text. If no blockers I'll open the RFC tomorrow. Anyone want to be a reviewer?

jun: happy to review.

ravi: +1, can help with runtime integration section.

maya: great — assigning reviewers in RFC. Closing thread for now.
